arxiv-2011-11849.title: Health-Focused Optimal Power Flow
arxiv-2011-11849.creator: Logesh Kumar, Parikshit Pareek, Sivakumar Nadarajan, Souvik Dasgupta, Amit Gupta, Hung D. Nguyen
arxiv-2011-11849.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a novel Health-Focused Optimal Power Flow (HF-OPF) to take into account the equipment health in operational and physical constraints. The health condition index is estimated based on the possible fault characteristics for generators and batteries.

arxiv-2202-03116.title: A novel wide-angle Compton Scanner setup to study bulk events in germanium detectors Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
arxiv-2202-03116.creator: I. Abt a, C. Gooch a, F. Hagemann a,e, L. Hauertmann a, D. Hervas Aguilar a2,a3,a, X. Liu a, O. Schulz a, M. Schuster a, A.J. Zsigmond a
arxiv-2202-03116.description: Abstract A novel Compton Scanner setup has been built, commissioned and operated at the Max-Planck-Institute for Physics in Munich to collect pulses from bulk events in high-purity germanium detectors for pulse shape studies. In this fully automated setup, the detector under test is irradiated from the top with 661.660 keV gammas, some of which Compton scatter inside the detector.

arxiv-2408-09550.title: Modeling net-charge fluctuations in heavy-ion collisions at the LHC
arxiv-2408-09550.creator: G.O. Ambaryan 1 , A.S. Chernyshov 1 , G.Kh. Eyyubova 2 , V.L. Korotkikh 2 , I.P. Lokhtin 2 , S.V. Petrushanko 2 , A.M. Snigirev 2,3 , and E.E. Zabrodin 2,4
arxiv-2408-09550.description: Abstract Analysis of P ​ b Pb + P ​ b Pb data for net-charge fluctuations at LHC energies using the hydjet++ model is presented. The strongly intensive quantities D D and Σ \Sigma were used to remove the effects related to system volume fluctuations. We employed two versions of hydjet++ for the analysis.

arxiv-2503-14631.title: An Ambiguous State Machine Thanks: This version: August 24, 2026
arxiv-2503-14631.creator: Matt Stephenson
arxiv-2503-14631.description: Abstract We show that a replicated state machine (such as a blockchain protocol) can retain liveness in a strategic setting even while facing substantial ambiguity over certain events. This is implemented by a complementary protocol called “Machine II”, which generates a non-ergodic value within chosen intervals such that no limiting frequency can be observed.

arxiv-2506-08954.title: Protriever: End-to-End Differentiable Protein Homology Search for Fitness Prediction
arxiv-2506-08954.creator: Ruben Weitzman, Peter Mørch Groth, Lood Van Niekerk, Aoi Otani, Yarin Gal, Debora S. Marks, Pascal Notin
arxiv-2506-08954.description: Abstract Retrieving homologous protein sequences is essential for a broad range of protein modeling tasks such as fitness prediction, protein design, structure modeling, and protein-protein interactions. Traditional workflows have relied on a two-step process: first retrieving homologs via Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSA), then training models on one or more of these alignments.

arxiv-2511-18524.title: Multiple change-points detection based on U U -Statistics under weak dependence
arxiv-2511-18524.creator: Joseph Ngatchou-Wandji, Echarif Elharfaoui, Michel Harel
arxiv-2511-18524.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Joseph Ngatchou-Wandji, Echarif Elharfaoui, Michel Harel. We study multiple change-points detection using multi-samples tests based on U U -statistics for absolutely regular observations. Our results extend those of Ngatchou-Wandji et al., 2022 concerned with the study of one single change-point. The asymptotic distributions of the test statistics under the null hypothesis and under a sequence of local alternatives are given explicitly, and the tests are shown to be consistent.

britannica-1911-simplon-pass.title: Simplon Pass (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-simplon-pass.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-simplon-pass.description: Article 'Simplon Pass' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 25), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. as a purely local route, the Simplon Pass rose into importance when Napoleon caused the carriage road to be built across it between 1800 and 1807, though it suffered a new eclipse on the opening of the Mont Cenis (1871) and St Gotthard railways (1882). The Simplon tunnel was opened in 1906.

plos-pone-0011854.description: PLOS ONE research article. There are no recent data on the prevalence and causes of blindness in the Occupied Palestinian Territories. pmc-10647572.title: Exosomes; a Potential Source of Biomarkers, Therapy, and Cure for Type-1 Diabetes
pmc-10647572.creator: Jonathan R T Lakey, Yanmin Wang, Michael Alexander, Mike K S Chan, Michelle B F Wong, Krista Casazza, Ian Jenkins, Abdelnaby Khalyfa
pmc-10647572.description: The scourge of type-1 diabetes (T1D) is the morbidity and mortality it and its complications cause at a younger age. This propels the constant search for better diagnostic, treatment, and management strategies, with the ultimate quest being a cure for T1D. Recently, the therapeutic potential of exosomes has generated a lot of interest.

pmc-11433020.title: Endochondral Ossification for Spinal Fusion: A Novel Perspective from Biological Mechanisms to Clinical Applications
pmc-11433020.creator: Rile Ge, Chenjun Liu, Yuhong Zhao, Kaifeng Wang, Xiluan Wang
pmc-11433020.description: Degenerative scoliosis (DS), encompassing conditions like spondylolisthesis and spinal stenosis, is a common type of spinal deformity. Lumbar interbody fusion (LIF) stands as a conventional surgical intervention for this ailment, aiming at decompression, restoration of intervertebral height, and stabilization of motion segments. Despite its widespread use, the precise mechanism underlying spinal fusion remains elusive.

pmc-12454868.title: Proteomic analysis of cerebrospinal fluid from females with multiple sclerosis highlights elevated microglial function and impaired neurogenesis
pmc-12454868.creator: Dean Oldham, Anthony Saviola, Enrique Alvarez, Kimberley D. Bruce
pmc-12454868.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune disorder of the central nervous system (CNS) that is characterized by demyelination, inflammation, and neurological damage. MS is the most common neurological disorder of young adults, negatively impacting their quality of life. Recent population-based estimates have determined that the prevalence of MS in the United States is growing and can be up to 3 times higher in females.

pmc-12468243.title: Deep Learning-Based Prediction Model of Surgical Indication of Nasal Bone Fracture Using Waters’ View
pmc-12468243.creator: Dong Yun Lee, Soo A Lim, Su Rak Eo, Konstantinos Seretis
pmc-12468243.description: Background/Objectives: The nasal bone is critical to both the functional integrity and esthetic contour of the facial skeleton. Nasal bone fractures constitute the most prevalent facial fracture presentation in emergency departments. The identification of these fractures and the determination of immediate intervention requirements pose significant challenges for inexperienced residents, potentially leading to oversight.

pmc-12529629.title: Integrated clinical research ensembles: A pathway to increased academic productivity
pmc-12529629.creator: Sergey Tarima, John R Meurer, David Friedland, Ndidiamaka Ojiako, Michael Anello, David Zimmerman, Renee McCoy, Reza Shaker
pmc-12529629.description: Introduction:The study objective was to evaluate whether the formation and funding of team science-guided Integrated Clinical Research Ensembles (ICREs) enhance individual faculty productivity, measured by publication and impact factor adjusted citation rates. The setting was a multi-institutional NIH Clinical and Translational Science Award-supported hub.

pmc-12988754.title: Subtype-Specific Causal Effects of Antidiabetic Drug Targets on Ovarian Cancer: Mendelian Randomization and Colocalization Evidence
pmc-12988754.creator: Enyu Tang, Jia Zeng, Xinlong Shi, Yani Wang, Yangchun Sun, Lingying Wu
pmc-12988754.description: BackgroundOvarian cancer (OC), characterized by a high mortality rate and limited treatment options, underscores the urgent need to identify novel therapeutic targets to advance individualized precision therapy. Exploring the potential of antidiabetic drug target genes as therapeutic candidates may expand the treatment repertoire of diverse OC subtypes.

pmc-13019291.title: Elimination of cis-cleavage in CRISPR diagnostics for one-pot rapid nucleic acid detection
pmc-13019291.creator: Wenhao Yin, Zhili Jin, Qingyuan Jiang, Shuqi Jin, Xinping Wang, Ruyi He, Bin Qiao, Jie Qiao, Xianhua Zhang, Yi Liu
pmc-13019291.description: Current one-pot clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats diagnostics are limited by the cis-cleavage activity of Cas nucleases, which leads to amplicon degradation during amplification. Here, we report a streamlined strategy that overcomes this limitation. By integrating a bipartite split-crRNA into Cas12a (SCas12a), we separate target recognition from PAM dependency and completely eliminate cis-cleavage while preserving robust trans-cleavage.

pmc-13072591.title: Perceptions of pediatric neurologists on the ideal candidate: a nationwide survey
pmc-13072591.creator: Ahmed Bamaga, Hebah Qashqari, Anas Alyazidi, Mohamed O E Babiker, Jihan Madani, Montaha Almudhry, Sulaiman Almobarak, Fatima Ismail
pmc-13072591.description: BackgroundPediatric neurology residency selection is increasingly holistic globally, yet the specific attributes prioritized by program directors (PDs) in Saudi Arabia and the United Arab of Emirates (UAE), where Saudi Commission for Health Specialties (SCFHS)-accredited programs are established, remain unexamined. This study investigates the perceptions of PDs, compared to non-PD pediatric neurologists, regarding the ideal candidate.

pmc-13192187.title: Mothers’ perceptions of bonding with their newborns in different care settings: a descriptive qualitative study
pmc-13192187.creator: Raymonde Gagnon, Diane St-Laurent, Amélie Garban, Carl Lacharité
pmc-13192187.description: BackgroundPregnancy and birth prepare the mother to enter into a relationship with and care for her baby, both through expectation of the child and the intense physiological hormonal changes associated with these processes. The birth environment likely plays a role in establishing the mother’s bond with the newborn.

pmc-13226347.title: A Highly Selective Hemicyanine-Based Turn-Off Fluorescent Sensor for Cyanide Detection in Food Samples
pmc-13226347.creator: Fuat Gokbel, Ziya Aydin, Şeyma Akın, Esma Nur Çenet, Mustafa Keles
pmc-13226347.description: Cyanide is a highly toxic anion. Humans are commonly exposed to cyanide through the consumption of drinking water or by eating plants that contain cyanogenic glucosides, such as cassava, a key carbohydrate source in many diets. While numerous methods exist for cyanide detection, few are both cost-effective and simple enough for use by individuals without specialized training.
